faq: Where does a cybersecurity audit start?
It starts with a review of your existing systems, access rights and backups. The result is a clear list of weak spots and priorities.
Does a small company need cybersecurity?

What cybersecurity measures should a company take first?

faq: What is an ERP system?

ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) is software that brings a company's internal operations — HR, finance, inventory, purchasing and sales — together in one system. The aim is for every department to work with the same data.
What is a CRM system and how is it different from ERP?

A CRM manages customer relationships and sales: the customer base, deal stages and tasks. An ERP covers the company's internal resources. In growing companies the two work together through integration.
Should we use a ready-made ERP platform or build a system from scratch?

If your processes are close to standard, customising a ready-made platform such as ERPNext is faster and more cost-effective. For a non-standard business model, a system built from scratch is a better fit.
What are the stages of CRM and ERP implementation?
Implementation moves through an audit, a pilot in one department, data migration, staff training and a phased rollout to the other departments.
Can a CRM or ERP be integrated with our existing software?
Yes: your website, payment systems, accounting and other services are connected via API.

faq: What is system integration?

System integration means connecting separate applications — a website, CRM and ERP, payment systems, government portals — so that they exchange data automatically. As a result, data is no longer copied by hand.
What is the difference between an API and a webhook?
An API is how one system asks another for data, while a webhook is a system sending a notification itself as soon as an event happens.
Which systems do you integrate?
We integrate payment gateways, government portals, ERP and CRM, accounting and inventory software, as well as single sign-on (SSO).
How do you make an integration reliable?
Through documentation, retrying failed requests, making sure repeated requests don't produce duplicate results (idempotency), and monitoring.

faq: What is IT outsourcing?
IT outsourcing means handing a company's IT functions — user support, servers, network, licences — over to an external team. Instead of keeping in-house staff, you get an agreed service level (SLA).
When does IT outsourcing make sense?

It makes sense when there isn't enough work for a full-time IT department, when you need expertise across several areas (network, servers, security), or when your existing IT employee needs reinforcing.
What is an SLA?
An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is an agreement that sets the response and resolution times for each type of request.
How does managed IT support work?
